text:
mona: heads up — ACME reported embeddings v1 vectors/sec dropped ~45% since ~03:00 UTC. tokens/sec for text gen is flat. they're seeing request latencies spike and queueing. attaching quick sample. :frowning:

jordan: can you paste the request headers + body? batch size, dims, model variant?

mona: sample request:
```json
{"model":"embed-v1","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":64}
```

dims reported by client: 1536. server model is embed-v1@1536-quant.

sachin: interesting that tokens/sec is stable but vectors/sec down. suggests vectorization path or post-process bottleneck (concat/IO) rather than raw GPU token generation. any recent infra changes?

mona: ops-bot deployed routing heuristic at 02:50 which increases batch coalescing for similar seq lengths. I rolled it back at 04:30 but spike started earlier.

jordan: can you share queue depth / executor metrics? `gpu_util`, `kvcache_hits`, `inflight_batches` for the time window?

mona: pulling flamegraphs now. brief metrics from 02:45-03:15 (summarized):
- gpu_util: 92% -> 95% (higher)
- vectors/sec: 120k -> 70k (down)
- tokens/sec: 800k -> 810k (flat)
- kvcache_mutex_waits: increased x6
- avg_batch_size: 58 -> 62

grace: kv-cache mutex waits up x6 — that smells like lock contention on the KV cache when many similar prefixes hit. If batching coalesced requests with same prefixes, could lead to serialized KV updates. That reduces vector throughput even if GPU busy.

jordan: repro idea: simulate many small unique vectors vs many repeated prefixes. run this locally on staging with `abtest-embed-load` job. also check `queue_time_ms` distribution; long tail would indicate head-of-line blocking.

mona: running repro now on staging: script:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"input":["prefix-$((i%10)) doc-$i"]}' &
done
wait
```

observed: kvcache_lock waits spike, vectors/sec dents, batch flushes delayed. logs show repeated `KVCache::acquire_lock` backoffs.

ops-bot: alert created: #incident-1977 kvcache-locks-high

sachin: probable root cause: new batch coalescing heuristic groups similar seq lengths and prefixes into same execution window which increases simultaneous KV cache access for identical keys; current KV cache locking is coarse-grained. On CPU side, lock contention serializes access so GPU can't consume KV fast enough -> effective vectors/sec drop and queue depth grows.

grace: short-term mitigation: 1) revert new coalescing (mona did partial rollback) 2) increase KV cache sharding (config knob `kvcache.shards`), 3) add exponential backoff jitter on KV lock backoff so threads don't thundering-herd. We should prioritize revert + config bump.

mona: applied config bump `kvcache.shards=32` to the affected pool and toggled coalescing off fully at 05:10 UTC. metrics show vectors/sec recovering to ~95% within 10m, queue depth dropping, mutex waits back to baseline. :thumbsup:

jordan: great. can you add repro steps + perf graphs to the incident ticket and open a follow-up engineering task to make KV lock fine-grained or switch to lockless CAS-based updates?

mona: done — linked graphs and the small staging script. created task ENG-7204 for KV rework and ENG-7205 for safer batch coalescing rollout + canary checks.

grace: action items: 
- ENG-7204: KV cache concurrency redesign (owner: sachin)
- ENG-7205: Coalescing rollout safety (owner: jordan)
- Ops: monitor kvcache_mutex_waits and vectors/sec for 48h (owner: mona)

sachin: will start KV sharding prototype tomorrow, ping me if you need perf counters or trace hooks.

mona: ping @acme support to confirm recovery. customer reports latencies back to normal for their traffic. closing incident but keeping watch for 48h. :eyes:

ingest-bot: archive thread in 7 days unless reopened.

jordan: nice catch, good triage team.
